issues.failure_explanation:
The paper presents \eqref{dL-new} as an equivalent reformulation of the Landau metric \eqref{dL}. The only support given is the analogy with Wasserstein ('This is analogous to the fact that the optimal vector field in 2-Wasserstein metric is the gradient of some potential function') followed by 'Then \eqref{dL-new} directly follows from \eqref{dL}'. Equality of the two infima requires a nontrivial projection/Hodge-type decomposition lemma: given an admissible pair (f,V) in \eqref{dL} with arbitrary V, one must show V can be replaced by a field 	ilde
abla\phi (equivalently, an arbitrary  u in \eqref{dL-new} can be replaced by a gradient) without increasing the cost while preserving the constraint. For the degenerate operator 	ilde
abla (projection \Pi(z), singular at z=0, acting on two-variable fields) this is a nontrivial statement; no such lemma is stated or proved, and the literal correspondence written (V=	ilde
abla\phi,  u=
abla\phi) is in addition sign-inconsistent (see ISSUE-001). The equivalence is therefore unsupported as written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the contained decomposition/projection lemma (for each admissible curve, project V onto the range of \tilde\nabla in the weighted space L^2(ff_*), showing the continuity constraint is preserved and the cost does not increase, i.e. a Hodge-type argument for the degenerate operator \tilde\nabla), or weaken the claim to an inequality between the two infima and restate the scheme accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that \eqref{dL-new} defines the same metric d_L as \eqref{dL} — the foundation for interpreting the Lagrangian/particle objectives \eqref{djko_L2}/\eqref{djko_p} as the Landau-metric JKO functional — is unproven; only one direction (\eqref{dL-new} ≤ \eqref{dL} via the explicit construction) is formally available, so the variational/gradient-flow interpretation advertised for the method is not established at the stated level of generality.
issues.title: Equivalence of the two Landau-metric formulations asserted without the required projection/decomposition argument
issues.why_classification: A contained but genuinely nontrivial missing lemma (decomposition for a degenerate two-variable operator) is needed; the repair is contained and a weakened inequality-level version leaves a comparable result, so it is more than minor but not a loss of architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: From A(z)(φ(v)−φ(v_*))=0 a.e. one only obtains that φ(v)−φ(v_*) lies in ker A(z)=span{z} for a.e. pair on supp f. The conclusion that φ is affine (in span{1,v}) on the support is a rigidity statement requiring a genuine argument (controlling increments over triples of support points, and a non-degeneracy assumption on supp f); it is asserted in a single line. Without it the lemma — and hence the reduction \eqref{opt_u}→\eqref{opt_u1} identifying the optimizer as score-plus-null-space — is unproven.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the classical rigidity argument (a.e.-parallel increments force φ = a + λv a.e. on supp f, using that the support is not contained in a line, or adding that hypothesis).
issues.overall_effect: The key structural conclusion of the JKO optimality analysis, \eqref{opt_u1} ('the unknown is a score plus a null-space term'), and the network-initialization rationale built on it, rest on a proof step that is asserted rather than established.
issues.title: Rigidity step in Lemma lemma_1 asserted without proof
issues.why_classification: A standard, contained rigidity lemma closes the gap; the conclusion and all downstream uses survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The sums in \eqref{djko_p2} and the updates \eqref{update_v}–\eqref{update_f} run over all ordered pairs (i,j), including i=j. For soft potentials the kernel A(z)=C_γ|z|^{γ+2}Π(z) is singular at z=0 (in the Coulomb case γ=−3, A(z)∝|z|^{-1}Π(z) blows up and Π(0) is undefined), so the diagonal terms h_{i,i} (and d_{i,i} as 0·A(0)) are undefined; the same occurs in the random-batch update of Section 4.3. Hence the variational particle problem \eqref{djko_p2} and the updates defining the method are not well defined for exactly the kernels used in the paper's physically relevant examples (Sections 5.3–5.4) unless a self-interaction convention (e.g. excluding j=i) is imposed, which the source never states.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the standard convention that self-interactions are omitted (sums restricted to j≠i, or A(0)-terms set to zero) in \eqref{djko_p}, \eqref{djko_p2}, \eqref{update_v}–\eqref{update_f} and the random-batch scheme; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The fully discrete scheme \eqref{djko_p2}–\eqref{update_f}, Algorithm algorithm_jko, and the random-batch update are not well posed for the Coulomb kernels used in the paper's main physical examples; the properties claimed in Propositions prop:added-3 and prop:added-4 are only meaningful once the convention is fixed.
issues.title: Particle JKO objective and update formulas ill-defined for singular (soft-potential/Coulomb) kernels
issues.why_classification: A one-line convention (exclude j=i) makes every quantity well defined; all guarantees, rates and experiments survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma sgd_lemma2's quadratic term carries the prefactor α_kL²B/(2N), but in the theorem's second displayed step it is combined with Δ ≤ α²N²/B²·((3M+2)‖∇ℓ‖²+3σ²) as if the prefactor were αL²/(2N), yielding the term (3σ²L²/2)α³N/B²; the correct product is (α_kL²B/2N)·(α_k²N²/B²)·3σ² = (3σ²L²/2)α_k³N/B. Telescoping therefore yields the noise floor 6σ²L²α²N/B, not the stated 6σ²L²α²N/B². The stated bound is a factor B stronger than the argument delivers and is not established by the proof (even with both lemmas repaired).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the factor B in the assembly and restate the conclusion with floor 6σ²L²α²N/B; the stated learning-rate smallness condition can be kept, so this is a contained restatement rather than a new proof.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised stochastic-convergence rate (the basis for claiming the shuffling SGD reduces the O(N²) JKO loss efficiently) is overstated by the factor B in the noise floor; the guarantee actually supported is ‖∇ℓ‖² averaged ≤ 4/(αK)[ℓ(θ0)−ℓ*] + 6σ²L²α²N/B.
issues.title: SGD convergence theorem: the displayed assembly drops a factor B, so the stated noise floor is overstated
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained correction plus a limited weakening of the constant (floor larger by the factor B); a recognizably comparable convergence guarantee survives, so it is more than a local fix but not a loss of the result type.

issues.failure_explanation: The last step needs ‖∇ℓ(θ_k) − ∇_θℓ_{ij}(θ^{(k+1)}_{q−1})‖ ≤ L√B‖θ_k−θ^{(k+1)}_{q−1}‖, which assumption (A.2) does not provide: (A.2) controls ‖∇ℓ_{ij}(θ₂)−∇ℓ_{ij}(θ_1)‖ for the same component, while the left side compares two different functions at two points and contains the sampling variance ‖∇ℓ(θ_k)−∇ℓ_{ij}(θ_k)‖, which does not vanish with ‖θ_k−θ^{(k+1)}_{q−1}‖ (take θ_{q−1}=θ_k: the left side is the variance, the right side is 0). The step is therefore an invalid inference; the stated bound is only recoverable by first averaging over the epoch (where the mean-zero variance parts cancel because each ordered pair appears in exactly one batch) and then applying smoothness termwise.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Route the estimate through the epoch average: ‖ḡ−∇ℓ(θ_k)‖² ≤ (1/(NB))Σ‖∇ℓ_{ij}(θ^{(k+1)}_{q−1})−∇ℓ_{ij}(θ_k)‖² (the mean-zero parts cancel because each ordered pair lies in exactly one batch), then apply (A.2) termwise; this reproduces exactly the stated prefactor α_kL²B/(2N).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma sgd_lemma2 — the descent step on which Theorem thm_opt_conv is built — is unproven as written, so the convergence analysis of Algorithm algorithm_opt is unreliable as written.
